# The register of vulnerabilities FerroEHR's manufacturer, Cadasto B.V., has
# reported to the maintainer of a component integrated in FerroEHR
# (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 Art 13(6)). One row per report, appended and
# never rewritten; a row is closed by filling its last two columns.
# A row is entered once the upstream advisory is public, or once the
# maintainer has declined one and the agreed disclosure date has passed, so a
# row never discloses a vulnerability before its fix. Until then the record is
# the upstream report itself. No row names a person: the maintainer is named
# by project, never by individual, and the correspondence stays outside the
# repository. The procedure is docs/post-market.md, "Vulnerabilities in
# integrated components".
# Columns:
#   id              U-<year>-<number>, in the order the reports were made
#   reported        the date the report went upstream, YYYY-MM-DD
#   component       the component and the affected versions, as its ecosystem names them (crate@version, image:tag)
#   channel         rustsec, ghsa (on the upstream repository), distro (a distribution's security tracker), or email
#   upstream_ref    the upstream advisory, issue or report identifier, once public
#   fix_shared      the pull request or patch offered upstream, or no
#   ferroehr_record the FerroEHR advisory, VEX statement or tracker issue that records the effect on FerroEHR
#   outcome         fixed upstream in <version>, declined, or no response, in one sentence, once closed
#   closed          the date it was closed, YYYY-MM-DD, once closed
